results.title: Patient-specific uncertainty calibration of deep learning-based ...
results.content: The uncertainty calibration of the OAR- or GTV-specific BM and PS models for each fraction image of each test patient was individually evaluated using reliability diagrams (Degroot and Fienberg 1983) and quantified through the expected calibration error (ECE), a standard scalar metric in machine learning to evaluate the discrepancy between predicted confidence levels and actual accuracy (Degroot and Fienberg 1983, Naeini *et al* 2015, Guo *et al* 2017, Nixon *et al* 2019). Post-training uncertainty calibration shifted the predicted probability values of voxels with high confidence toward greater uncertainty (i.e. closer to a predicted probability of 0.5; visible in the histograms in the last column), resulting in increased relOU values: from 11% (BM) to 25% (calBM) for the population-based models and from 8.5% (PS) to 18% (calPS) for the patient-specific fine-tuned models.
